text:
Elaine R: heads-up — ap-south applied a default-deny egress rule to infra-subnets about 5m ago. keystore -> kms proxy is returning 504s and GPU warm pool nodes are failing to join. seeing a backlog in the scheduler.
Tom K: ack. seeing same in the dashboard (ap-south). warmup queue length +120, nodes stuck in Init. Any recent firewall changes?
Mohit P: @Elaine R can you paste the fw rule id? iirc security was rolling a tighter egress policy but that shouldn't have hit privnet yet.
Elaine R: rule id fw-rule-az3-2026. quick curl from a staging pod: `curl -v https://keystore-proxy.internal:8443/health` -> `* Connection timed out` then `504` from our side.
Jules (security): that rule was part of the egress hardening canary for ap-south. it was scoped to deny all outbound except approved list; looks like keystore-proxy ip range wasn't added. cc @ops-bot for temporary exception? :exclamation:
ops-bot: Incident created: #inc-1745601111. Priority: P2. Suggested temp-mitigation: add keystore-proxy IPs to allowlist OR open specific egress to kms proxy FQDN.
Tom K: we need a quick mitigation to bring GPU nodes online — can we allow the keystore-proxy ELB range and restart warm pool join?
Mohit P: I can patch security group to allow 10.12.32.0/28 -> keystore-proxy:8443 for 30m. will also update runbook. running: `aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-boot --cidr 10.12.32.0/28 --protocol tcp --port 8443`
Elaine R: doing a rolling restart of the warm pool controller after patch: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/warm-pool-controller -n infra`
deploy-bot: deploy/warm-pool-controller restarted (revision v2.4.7) — monitoring joins.
Tom K: after allowlist and restart we're seeing node joins start again. backlog down to +12. good signal. need postmortem and a way to avoid manual allowlists.
Jules (security): agreed. two action items: 1) update egress canary definition to include keystore-proxy ranges before rollout; 2) add automated smoke test that attempts keystore egress from a join-flow pod in staging and blocks rollout on failures.
Mohit P: also raising a short-term tradeoff: we could relax audit exporter egress for 30m so warmup traffic wins, but that increases audit log shipping cost and slightly reduces retention guarantees. prefer allowlist route.
Elaine R: created follow-ups: https://redwood-infra/runbooks/keystore-egress-checklist and PR to ops-config to add IPs to canary whitelist (link: https://github.com/redwood/ops-config/pull/472).
Jules (security): please include IAM boundary check — there was a role-boundary tighten last week that affected the keystore proxy's assume-role TTL; confirm no related auth failures.
Tom K: verified assume-role still valid; logs show only network-level 504s.
ops-bot: incident #1745601111 updated: mitigation applied, monitoring healthy, will close pending 1h stability window. :white_check_mark:
Mohit P: after action: we should evaluate cost of keeping exception vs extending canary cadence. scheduling a 30m sync with security and infra to decide next steps.
Elaine R: thanks everyone. leaving the temporary allowlist for now, will revert after postmortem and put in a safer rollout path. :thumbsup:
